newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH signals softer stance toward British groups.
newsitem.headline: LVMH signals softer stance toward British groups.

text.p: French luxury group LVMH indicated Monday that it might accept as little as 25 percent of the drinks company it wants to create with Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc.
The French group's conciliatory stance, expressed in a newspaper controlled by LVMH Chairman Bernard Arnault, was interpreted by analysts as being part of the preliminaries to negotiations.
Analysts said that despite harsh exchanges Friday, when Guinness and GrandMet slammed Arnault's proposal, it remained in everyone's interest to reach a settlement.
Arnault initially demanded 35 percent in the potential new group, which he has dubbed Drinksco, a stake characterised as unreasonable by the British groups.

LVMH recently said the stake was negotiable, and analysts speculated Arnault would hold out for 30 percent of the group -- whose portfolio would include the Hennessy, Moet & Chandon, J&B, Smirnoff, Gilbey's, Tanquery, Johnnie Walker and Gordon brands.
Analysts said Arnault looked weakened after the British groups' detailed rebuttal of his claims.
